skills.name: Image Component Optimization
skills.description: Optimize image delivery by implementing lazy loading and automatic device-based resizing. Use when rendering images in responsive web layouts to reduce initial page load time and improve performance.
skills.skill_body: Apply the Image Component to abstract image optimization complexity. The component lazy-loads images on viewport entry and automatically resizes based on device screen size. Ensure images are wrapped with the Image Component rather than native tags to enable these optimizations. ## Objective optimize_image_delivery ## Applicable Signals - rendering images in responsive web layouts - need to reduce initial page load time - multiple images on a single page - images of varying sizes across device breakpoints ## Contraindications - static images with fixed dimensions that do not require responsiveness - images already served from CDN with built-in optimization - critical above-the-fold images where lazy loading would delay visibility ## Intervention Moves - Replace native elements with Image Component - Configure device-based sizing rules - Verify lazy-load behavior on viewport entry ## Workflow Steps - Identify images in the layout that would benefit from lazy loading and responsive resizing - Replace native tags with Image Component - Configure device-based sizing parameters - Test lazy-load behavior and responsive resizing across target devices ## Constraints - Image Component must be used instead of native tags to enable optimization - Device size detection must be available in the rendering environment ## Cautions - Lazy loading may delay image visibility; consider eager loading for critical above-the-fold images - Automatic resizing requires device size context; verify breakpoint configuration matches design requirements ## Output Contract - Images load lazily on viewport entry - Image dimensions adapt to device screen size without layout shift - Page load time is reduced compared to native implementation

skills.name: Link Prefetching Strategy
skills.description: Prefetch linked pages in the background to enable faster and smoother page transitions. Use when implementing internal page links to reduce perceived latency during navigation.
skills.skill_body:
When a user hovers over or focuses on an internal link, prefetch the target page's resources in the background. This allows the page transition to complete without visible loading delay when the user clicks. Do not prefetch external links or heavy resources in bandwidth-constrained environments.

## Objective

accelerate_navigation
## Applicable Signals

- Internal link element detected
- Page transition latency is a performance concern
- User interaction with link is imminent

## Contraindications

- External links to third-party domains
- Links to heavy resources that should not be preloaded
- Bandwidth-constrained or metered network environments
- User has disabled prefetching preferences

## Intervention Moves

- Configure Link component to prefetch target page resources
- Trigger prefetch on user hover or focus event

## Workflow Steps

- Identify internal navigation links in the application
- Configure Link component to prefetch target page resources
- Trigger prefetch on user hover or focus event
- Complete page transition on user click without additional loading

## Constraints

- Only prefetch internal links within the application
- Respect user network conditions and data-saver preferences
- Do not prefetch resources that are not necessary for immediate page load

## Cautions

- Excessive prefetching may consume unnecessary bandwidth
- Monitor prefetch success rate to avoid wasted resources

## Output Contract

- Target page resources are prefetched before user click; page transition completes without visible loading delay.
